description: The line ClaudeService writes on the claude CLI's stdin for one call, compared as JSON (key order and escaping are the writer's; HK-395). A user turn is {type: user, message: {role: user, content: [{type: text, text}]}, parent_tool_use_id: null} with the text trimmed; a control request is always the nested envelope {type: control_request, request_id, request: {subtype, …}}, never the flat shape, which makes the CLI exit 1 (DESIGN.md v1.1 A). interrupt carries no value, set_model carries model and set_permission_mode carries mode, trimmed. A call whose text or value trims to nothing writes nothing (null). Every line ends with one newline. An unknown subtype (set_effort) is not a call the app makes; verified live, the CLI answers it with an error and keeps running.
function: What ClaudeService writes on stdin for one call (CoreBridge.claudeUserTurnLine / claudeControlRequestLine) ↔ powerup_core::harness::claude::stdin — input {call: "send"|"interrupt"|"setModel"|"setPermissionMode", text?|model?|mode?, requestID?}; expected: the JSON object of the line, or null when nothing is written
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.1 A (verified live against claude CLI v2.1.243); Tests/PowerUpTests/HarnessFixtureTests.swift testClaudeStdinTable plays it through CoreBridge.claudeUserTurnLine and claudeControlRequestLine, the writers behind ClaudeService since slice 2.3. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/harness.rs claude_stdin_cases runs user_turn_line and control_request_line.
capturedAgainst: The Swift parser (JSONSerialization) of PowerUp at 7404080, built with Swift 5.9.2 (Xcode 15.2) and run on macOS 27.2; the wire shapes themselves were verified live against claude CLI v2.1.243 (DESIGN.md v1.1 A)

cases.name: a user turn
cases.reason: Verified live: a user turn is this envelope and a newline (HK-069).

cases.name: the turn text is trimmed at both ends only
cases.reason: Inner line breaks and indentation are the person's text (HK-069).

cases.name: quotes, slashes, CJK and emoji survive
cases.reason: The text reaches the CLI exactly; escaping is the writer's job (HK-069).

cases.name: a whitespace-only turn sends nothing
cases.reason: An empty turn would start a turn about nothing (HK-069).

cases.name: a zero-width-space turn sends nothing
cases.reason: Swift's trim removes U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE too (Foundation's whitespacesAndNewlines, measured on macOS 27.2), so an invisible turn is an empty one (HK-069).

cases.name: interrupt
cases.reason: Verified live: the nested envelope with a request_id; the flat shape kills the CLI (HK-067).

cases.name: set_model carries the trimmed model
cases.reason: set_model carries model; the value is trimmed (HK-068).

cases.name: an empty model sends nothing
cases.reason: An empty value sends no request (HK-068).

cases.name: a zero-width-space model sends nothing
cases.reason: The model is trimmed with the same set as a turn, U+200B included (HK-068).

cases.name: a whitespace mode sends nothing
cases.reason: A value that trims to nothing sends no request (HK-068).

cases.name: the request id is passed through
cases.reason: Any unique string works as a request id (DESIGN.md v1.1 A, verified live with R1 and R2).
